evidence.quoted_text:
def claim_run_dir(self):
        base = Path(self.args.record_dir)
        resolved = base.resolve()
        root = self.root.resolve()
        require(resolved != root and root not in resolved.parents,
                "--record-dir must be outside the deployment checkout")
        base.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        require(not base.stat().st_mode & 0o077,
                "private record directory must have mode 0700: " + str(base))
        name = ("run-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
                + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
        self.run_dir = base / name
        self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
        return self.run_dir
evidence.reason: `claim_run_dir` creates the record base and `self.run_dir` with `mkdir`, then returns without fsyncing the containing directory. The later `durable_write(path, receipt)` only makes the receipt and its run directory durable; it does not persist the new run-directory entry in `base` (nor `base`'s own entry when it is newly created). A power loss can therefore leave admission/host-held state while losing the recovery record that holds `prior_sha` and trigger state. This is an implementation gap in the stated recovery-evidence durability, not a new requirement.
